'''Humphrey John Maris''' (April 25, 1939 – July 28, 2025) was an American-British physicist and a professor at [[Brown University]] from 1965 to 2014. He specialized in research on low-temperature physics and ultrafast ultrasonics.<ref name="Innovation"/> 

He attended [[Imperial College London]] receiving a B.Sc. degree in 1960 and a Ph.D. in 1963.<ref name="Duke"/> He was a postdoctoral fellow at [[Case Western Reserve University|Case Institute of Technology]] from 1963 to 1965.<ref name="Duke"/> In 1965 he became a professor at Brown.<ref name="Brown"/> In 1991 he was made the George Chase Professor of Natural Science.<ref name="Brown"/> He led experiments into the nature of the [[quantum state]] of the [[electron]].<ref name="electron"/> His patent on a method of nondestructive evaluation of semiconductors is widely used.<ref name="Innovation"/> He retired in 2014.<ref name="Brown"/> He died of complications of Parkinson's Disease in 2025.<ref name="obituary"/>

== Honors and awards ==
Maris has received the following honors and awards.<ref name="Researcher"/><ref name="Brown"/>
* UK Science Research Council Fellowship, 1972
* Japanese Society for Promotion of Science Senior Fellowship, 1982
* Senior Alexander Von Humboldt Award,1989
* Japanese Society for Promotion of Science Senior Fellowship, 2003
* Brown University Award for Technical Innovation and Commercialization, 2005
* Prize for Phonon Physics, (Klemens award) 2007
* Phillip J. Bray Award for Excellence in Teaching in the physical sciences, 2009
* [[Fritz London Memorial Prize|Fritz London Memorial Award]] for Low Temperature Physics, 2011
* Brown Technology Innovation Impact Award, 2023
